limitations: Retain generated Compiler/Windvale/*-Artifact-* readers. The emitter project consumes them and Generate-Compiler-Artifact-Readers.mjs owns their bounded generation. The prior diagnostic correction records a passing 14-file generation check; this unchanged generation boundary was not rebuilt for prose edits.

Retain immutable Stage 0 recovery metadata. Managed source is already absent from main; Bootstrap/Stage0/README.md and the retirement inventory name the exact required recovery release. Archival provenance is not an obsolete production compiler.

Retain Source-Edition-Predecessor-Core.mjs and its pinned source identity. Current-Split-Compiler-Cache-Core.mjs invokes it to construct modern Project 4 tools through the accepted historical predecessor. The active native preparation run actually consumes this path. Removing it would break current construction.

Retain paired host launchers for registered owners, including Test-Compiler-Split-Development.cmd/.sh and Test-Language-1.0-Front-Door.cmd/.sh. Invoke-WindvaleTests.ps1 deliberately selects .cmd on Windows and .sh on Linux, with executable validation. Their host roles are distinct even when thin wrappers share a Node implementation.

Retain Build-Current-Wvb and Build-Cached-Project-Wvb host entry points. The former owns the pinned build driver and normal Project 4 publication dispatch; the latter owns reusable development construction and Project 4 current split dispatch. Development-Owner-Dependencies.txt records reconstruction, database, generic and front-door consumers. Similar names do not make their contracts interchangeable.

Retain the full legacy front-door owner and its 495 registered cases. Its development subset and later supplied-product selectors do not subsume every frozen-input, source-profile or descriptor boundary. The known old emission-rejection expectation needs reconciliation against its selected product, not wholesale test deletion. Verification consolidation remains item 4.

Preserve valid caches, ignored diagnostic products and in-use temporary checkouts. They contain measured evidence or active construction dependencies. This audit did not purge them or assert that all ignored files are disposable.

The scope is the named candidates raised by this simplification program, not every file in the repository. No unused-code conclusion is inferred from the absence of a text search hit. Historical qualification and support contracts are unchanged. No broad compiler/runtime verification was run for this editorial and retention audit.
